AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 4, 2020
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-25-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE CLOSED TO THE
PUBLIC AND VIDEOCONFERENCED. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN
EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR CALL (571) 317-3122; ACCESS CODE: 156-198-269
DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM OR UNDER ORAL COMMUNICATIONS. THE MEETING
MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  VIDEOCONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957: THREAT
  TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County
  Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: APN 8056-017-901; Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the
  City and Penny Reeves, Norwalk Auto Auction; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8 – Property: 12801 Rosecrans; Negotiating parties: Scott Sheldon, on behalf of the City and
  Glen Emanuel of Evergreen Media, LLC; Under Negotiation: price and terms of payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  John Ramirez
  Director of Community Development

FLAG SALUTE
  Richard Rojas
  Deputy City Manager

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS - None.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS
  COVID-19 Update.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of July 21,
  2020 and July 29, 2020. 825-04

  Minutes
 2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period June 28, 2020 – July 11,
  2020, in the total amount of $942,344.58. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period July
  15, 2020 through July 28, 2020, in the total amount of $6,703,961.74. 640

  Report

4.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – JULY 22, 2020 - No action is required unless the City Council
  elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the Commission’s
  action was final. 320

  Synopsis

5.  AGREEMENT – PARKING PERMIT PROGRAM MANAGEMENT AT THE NORWALK/SANTA FE
  SPRINGS TRANSPORTATION CENTER METROLINK STATION - Staff recommends City Council
  approve an agreement with iNet, Inc. dba iParq for the Permit Parking Program Management at the
  Norwalk/Santa Fe Springs Metrolink Station for the term of July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, with
  two (2) additional one (1) year periods from July 1st through June 30th of each year thereafter; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and extensions, provided there is funding in the
  budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 920-10-01

  Report

6.  AMENDMENT NO. 1 – PURCHASE FOUR CHARGEPOINT CHARGING EQUIPMENT FOR ZERO
  EMISSION BUSES - Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 1 with Gillig, LLC
  increasing the total amount from $3,797,676 to $4,057,455 to acquire the four (4) ChargePoint CPE250
  charging equipment; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, provided there is
  funding on the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 634-03

  Report

7.  AWARD CONTRACT - COUNCIL CHAMBER AUDIO/VIDEO UPGRADE PROJECT - Staff
  recommends City Council award a contract to EIDIM in the amount of $107,140 for the Council
  Chambers Audio/Video Upgrade Project; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement
  and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney.

  Report

8.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT – BUCKNAM AND ASSOCIATES - UTILITIES PROGRAM
  MANAGEMENT AND UTILITIES ENGINEERING SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve
  the agreement with Bucknam and Associates to provide Utilities Program Management and Utilities
  Engineering Services in the amount of $65,520; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City in a
  form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

9.  AMENDMENT NO. 6 TO AGREEMENT WITH EDINGTON, PEEL & ASSOCIATES INC. FOR
  FEDERAL ADVOCACY SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 6 to the
  agreement with Edington, Peel & Associates Inc. extending the term through June 30, 2022 in the
  amount of $51,000 annually for federal advocacy services; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  the amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 120-01

  Report

10. RESOLUTION NO. 20-56 – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 BUDGET - NORWALK SENIOR
  NUTRITION PROGRAM - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-56, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING AN AMENDMENT
  TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ADOPTED BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE FUNDS TO COVER STAFF
  COSTS FOR THE NORWALK SENIOR NUTRITION PROGRAM DURING FISCAL YEAR 2020/21, in
   the amount of $175,293. 425-02-03/610

  Report

  11. ORDINANCE NOS. 20-1717 – ADOPTING ZONE CHANGE NO. 361; 20-1718 – ADOPTING A
  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT – FIRESTONE BOULEVARD CUL-DE-SAC SOUTH OF
  ROSECRANS AVENUE – Staff recommends City Council accept for second reading and adopt:

  a.  Ordinance No. 20-1717, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS
  FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION APPROVING ZONE CHANGE NO. 361; and

  b.  Ordinance No. 20-1718, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING A
  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF NORWALK AND EVERGREEN MEDIA
  LLC APPROVING A NEW DIGITAL BILLBOARD SIGN ON FIRESTONE BOULEVARD SOUTH
  OF ROSECRANS AVENUE ADJACENT TO THE I-5 FREEWAY. 320-09-361/925-13

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  12. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

  13. CERTIFIED LIST - PERSONNEL APPEALS BOARD – Staff recommends City Council choose from the
  available options:

  a.  Confirm all the current appointments, assigning Ms. Boltz to either Councilmember Ramirez or
  Valencia;

  b.  Fill the vacancy by either Councilmember Ramirez or Valencia;

  c.  Vacate some/all members and make appointment(s). 255-01

  Report

REPORTS

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 20-57 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – PROJECT NO. 7241 - TRAFFIC SIGNAL
  WARRANT STUDY AND CONCEPTUAL DESIGN SERVICES - STUDEBAKER ROAD AT HALCOURT
  AVENUE - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 20-57, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE MEASURE M FUNDS FOR PROJECT NO. 7241 - TRAFFIC
  SIGNAL WARRANT STUDY AND CONCEPTUAL DESIGN AT STUDEBAKER ROAD AND
  HALCOURT AVENUE, in the amount of $37,000; and

  b.  approve an agreement with Zimmerman Engineering, in the amount of $29,295 to provide design
  services for Project No. 7241, Traffic Signal Warrant Study and Conceptual Design Services, for
  Studebaker Road at Halcourt Avenue; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement
  and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7241

  Report

  15. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – AUGUST EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive
  and file.

  Report

  16. URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 20-1719U – ESTABLISHING PROCEDURES FOR TEMPORARY OR
  PERMANENT HOUSING FOR PERSONS EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS OR PERSONS WHO
   TEST POSITIVE FOR COVID-19 OR THOSE WHO HAVE HAD HIGH-RISK EXPOSURE – Staff
  recommends City Council adopt by title only Ordinance No. 20-1719U, AN URGENCY ORDINANCE
  OF THE CITY OF NORWALK, CALIFORNIA ESTABLISHING PROCEDURES FOR LOCAL
  CONSULTATION AND COORDINATION BETWEEN THE CITY AND THE STATE, COUNTY, AND/OR
  OTHER PUBLIC AGENCIES INTENDING TO ESTABLISH, IMPLEMENT, OR OPERATE
  TEMPORARY OR PERMANENT HOUSING FOR PERSONS EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS OR
  PERSONS WHO TEST POSITIVE FOR COVID-19 OR THOSE WHO HAVE HAD HIGH-RISK
  EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 TO BE PLACED AT HOTELS, MOTELS, OR OTHER PUBLIC AND
  PRIVATE FACILITIES LOCATED WITHIN THE CITY OF NORWALK, and waive further reading.

  Report

  Ordinance

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated July 31, 2020.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
